description: Provenance of orbits.json for the Orbits playground.

gaia_query.adql:
SELECT source_id, ref_epoch, ra, dec, parallax, parallax_error, pmra, pmra_error, pmdec, pmdec_error, radial_velocity, radial_velocity_error, rv_nb_transits, rv_template_teff, grvs_mag, ruwe, phot_g_mean_mag, bp_rp, parallax_pmra_corr, parallax_pmdec_corr, pmra_pmdec_corr
FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source
WHERE source_id IN (3507879565090229888, 5853498713190525696, 4472832130942575872, 762815470562110464, 4810594479418041856, 6268770373590148224)
gaia_query.note: Gaia DR3 reference epoch J2016.0; the archive reported release 3.15 at query time

solar.note: distance from the Sun to the Galactic centre 8.0 kpc and circular speed 220 km/s, the normalisation of MWPotential2014 (Bovy 2015); height of the Sun above the plane 20.8 pc (Bennett and Bovy 2019, MNRAS 482, 1417); solar peculiar motion (U, V, W) = (11.10, 12.24, 7.25) km/s (Schoenrich, Binney and Dehnen 2010, MNRAS 403, 1829), so the Sun's Galactocentric velocity is (11.10, 232.24, 7.25) km/s. Frame: astropy Galactocentric, right-handed, x from the Sun towards the centre, y along Galactic rotation, z towards the north Galactic pole; the Sun sits at x = -8 kpc
solar.distance_note: distances are 1 / parallax; every selected star has parallax / error above 600. No parallax zero-point correction is applied: the Lindegren et al. (2021) offsets are of order -0.02 mas, 0.1 percent of the smallest parallax here

coordinates.uncertainties: standard deviation over 20000 draws of (parallax, pmra, pmdec, radial velocity) from a multivariate normal with the Gaia errors and the three published correlation coefficients; seed 20261026

reference_orbits.method: galpy Orbit from the same SkyCoord with ro = 8 kpc, vo = 220 km/s, zo = 0.0208 kpc, solarmotion = [-11.1, 12.24, 7.25]; integrated for 10 Gyr in MWPotential2014 with dop853_c on 200,001 output times
reference_orbits.sign_convention: galpy's L_z is positive for rotation with the disc; in the astropy frame of orbits.json that is -(x v_y - y v_x). The page uses galpy's sign
reference_orbits.energy_convention: energy_km2_s2 is galpy's orbit energy shifted so that the potential is zero at infinity (galpy's value is kept as energy_galpy_km2_s2); see potential_checks.Phi_zero_point_km2_s2

potential_checks.zero_point_note: galpy's values of Phi below include this constant; the page's potential is zero at infinity, so page values equal galpy values minus the constant. Forces are unaffected
potential_checks.radius_note: galpy's eccentricity, rperi and rap use the spherical radius sqrt(R^2 + z^2); the page computes its live values the same way
